title: Competitive risk scanner: integrate model availability signals, pricing telemetry, and latency degradation detectors
creator: Asha Moreno
description:
Objective: Build a lightweight scanner that fuses externally observable signals about third-party model providers into a single competitive risk score for Redwood product teams. The scanner will ingest model availability indicators (endpoint errors, time-to-first-byte, region outages), public pricing telemetry, and latency degradation patterns to surface early procurement and routing risks.

Scope:
- Ingest (near-realtime) public API health signals from a configurable provider list (initially 8 providers across NA/EU/APAC).
- Normalize price and token-cost signals from published rate cards and community-scraped telemetry.
- Detect sustained latency degradations (10%+ P95 increase vs baseline for >5 minutes) and translate to a risk vector.
- Output: daily risk score per provider-model-region and a summarized alert for score > 0.7 (0..1 scale).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Data pipeline ingests three signal types and stores 30-day rolling snapshots.
2) Model-level risk score computed and exposed via an internal dashboard with drilldowns (model, region, signal contribution).
3) Alerting integration to Slack channel #pm-model-risk and webhook to SRE runbook for high-severity events.
4) Initial evaluation report comparing scanner alerts to two historical incidents (Q4 provider outage and APAC latency spike) with precision/recall > 0.6.

Trade-offs & decisions:
- We will use passive, externally observable telemetry only (no contractual access) to avoid legal/compliance overhead. This limits depth but reduces friction.
- Aggregation window is 5 minutes for latency feeders to avoid noisy signals; longer windows considered in follow-ups for lower-sensitivity use-cases.
- Scoring model is intentionally simple (weighted sum) for interpretability; future iteration may add ML-based anomaly fusion if useful.

Data sources & artifacts:
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.com/confluence/display/PM/competitive-risk-scanner (draft)
- Prototype notebook (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-risk-proto
- Dashboard mockup (Looker): https://looker.redwood.internal/dashboards/pm-risk-scanner-proto
- GitHub prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/signal-fusion/pull/42

Metrics to track: ingestion latency, false-alert rate, time-to-detect high-severity events, usage by PM/Eng (weekly active viewers), and downstream routing changes triggered by scanner alerts.

Next steps:
- [Week 1] Wire up three data collectors: public health endpoints, scraped pricing, and synthetic latency prober. (Owner: Eng-data)
- [Week 2] Implement scoring pipeline and internal API. (Owner: Backend)
- [Week 3] Dashboard + Slack webhook, run retrospective on historical incidents. (Owner: Analytics + SRE)

2026-03-07: Backend raised a dependency on ENG-314159 for the internal time-series store. Eng-systems suggested a short-lived S3-backed store for the MVP to avoid infra queue. Accepting S3 for MVP.
2026-03-09: Design review with Analytics — dashboard wireframes approved with drilldown by region/model and contributor signal bars. Need link to runbook text for high-severity alerts.
2026-03-10: SRE reviewed alerting thresholds. Recommended adding a cooldown (30 minutes) to avoid alert storms during transient GLBs. Will add to scoring config.
notes: This ticket is intended to reduce surprise provider outages hitting Hosted API customers and to inform routing/fallback policies. Keep the first iteration narrow and instrument signal quality carefully.
